C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-3.IntentSummary:
Author the execution for the approved, frozen spec `.ngrace/changes/active/C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-3/spec.xml` and only within it; the plan conforms to the spec, it does not extend, narrow or reinterpret it. One deliverable file, `src/artifact/xml.test.ts`, three repairs in one bundle (`D11`: nothing is deferred, and nothing needs to be): R1 — a digit-free non-vacuity assertion in the pairing test named `pairs every element of the real record files at their committed bytes`; R2 — the index relation re-derived under exactly the shipped engine's live-`Entry` predicate; R3 — the anti-occupancy guard reimplemented over the TypeScript parser the file already imports, the hand-rolled scanner removed, and the guard's discriminating directions shipped as synthetic self-tests. The record is this bundle's read, never its write: no task writes any record file, the engine, or any governed surface outside the one file (`AC-RECORD-UNTOUCHED`, `AC-NO-SRC-BEYOND-REPAIR`), and the plan's `ObservedWriteScope` is exactly that one file.
T1 — the repairs, measured at this plan's commit `9573f5e3dffa163d34446e162cd534afe9694670` (branch `c-flush-and-pay`, tree clean apart from this bundle's own artifacts). The spec's base commit `74f706aa1f26d95687c2fb23fa179351dfde9e33` is this commit's parent, and the supersede commit between them touched only `.ngrace/changes/` paths (measured: the diff between the two commits moves `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-2` to its archive home and arrives this bundle's spec — no `src/` or `scripts/` byte moves), so the byte-invariance commands below name the spec's base and see exactly the surface they charter. The shipped control at both commits: `bun test src/artifact/xml.test.ts` — 26 pass / 0 fail, 2009 expect() calls, exit 0 (driven on a throwaway copy of the base and in this tree). R1: the pairing test's per-file loop binds a node list per file (`src/artifact/xml.test.ts:619` at the base commit) and only iterates it, so an empty list satisfies the whole test; measured on a throwaway copy, renaming every `<Finding>` element of `findings.xml` (210 direct children, measured by the shipped parser over direct children; root open and close tags untouched) leaves the shipped suite green — 26 pass / 0 fail, 1589 expect() calls, exit 0 — the 420 missing expectations being the hollowed elements' per-element assertions, silently skipped. The repair is the spec's chartered digit-free form: destructure the first element of the bound list (`const [firstGenreChild] = nodes;`) and require it defined (`expect(firstGenreChild, \`${file}:${tag} carries at least one element\`).toBeDefined();`) — a form carrying no numeric literal, so the shipped guard's numeric-literal scan over the body stays green on it. R2: the test derives the live index `Entry` set by `entry.attributes.layer === "live"` (`src/artifact/xml.test.ts:657` at the base commit); the engine derives it by `entry.attributes.layer !== "retired"` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:996`, the `liveEntryCount` metric at :991-997), the metric the persist path consumes (:1260 — `persistSnapshot` at :950 returns the `{ base, headroom, ceiling }` snapshot that `withRootSnapshot` writes, so :1260 is the thing that actually persists `base`) and the ceiling check consumes (:1439, `checkCeilingValue` at :1514 comparing only `liveSize > ceiling` and never re-deriving the persisted `base`). The repair holds the engine's predicate exactly — no stricter and no looser filter. R3: the shipped guard is a hand-rolled lexer (`scanCode` :753, `pairingBodySpan` :724, `moduleBindingInitializer` :900, and the `NUMERIC_LITERAL_SHAPE` / `OCCUPANCY_TABLE_SHAPE` / `MODULE_BINDING_SHAPE` shapes at :679-681); measured evadable by an initializer holding its number behind an internal semicolon, false-red on a cosmetic `async` reformat of the pairing callback, and blind to destructured names and non-first declarators; the file already imports and uses the TypeScript parser (`import ts from "typescript"` :5, `ts.createSourceFile` :393 inside `collectFromText` :392). The replacement guard reads guarded source with that parser: numeric literals inside the pairing test's callback body read from the parser's numeric-literal nodes; the occupancy-table field shape (a member named `expected` typed `number`) anywhere in the file in interface/type-literal and labeled-tuple form; module-scope bindings with numeric initializers referenced from the body, every declarator visited and each initializer examined in full as an expression node; the refusal clause kept.
T2 — the budgets, and why two tasks. The shipped budgets re-read at this plan's commit: `FIX_SIGNATURE_REPEAT_BUDGET = 2` (`src/grace-cursor.ts:187`) and `FIX_DISTINCT_SIGNATURE_BUDGET = 4` (`src/grace-cursor.ts:193`), evaluated per task over failed-attempt signatures collected after the last resolving resume (`src/grace-cursor.ts:1809`-1821), firing trigger R when the same kind+key signature appears this many times and trigger D when that many distinct signatures accumulate (`decideFixBudgetEscalation`, `src/grace-cursor.ts:1827`). The plan carries two tasks: T-001 lands R1 and R2, T-002 lands R3. Measured basis: the intermediate state — R1 and R2 applied, the shipped guard untouched — is green (`bun test src/artifact/xml.test.ts`: 26 pass / 0 fail, 2016 expect() calls, exit 0, driven on a throwaway copy), so T-001 is a demonstrable milestone and not a green-but-undemonstrated boundary, and its probes run before T-002 starts. The two repairs' failure signatures (pairing content and its record-copy probes) and the guard's (locator and detector behaviour, and its synthetic directions) are distinct families over the same file, the same suite and the same write scope: separate tasks give each family its own budget window, so guard iteration cannot consume the relations' budget and vice versa, and neither task needs the other's reserve. Both budgets bind each task's verification cycle independently; neither is changed by this bundle.
T3 — the suites' root binding, and what it permits and forbids for probes. The pairing test resolves the production record from its own tree — `path.resolve(import.meta.dir, "..", "..", "docs", "plans", "active", "RM-GOVERNED-PATH")` (`src/artifact/xml.test.ts:601` at the base commit) — and the retirement suite resolves the record under its own `import.meta.dir`'s parent; neither suite takes a record path, so every suite-level probe runs on a throwaway copy of the REPOSITORY with the copy's record or test file mutated and the suite run inside the copy, never against the committed tree; the shipped CLI validator takes a record directory argument (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts`, positional with `repoRoot` from the process cwd) and is driven from inside the same copies.
T4 — the mapping obligation, measured. The spec's evidence-hygiene Constraint fixes the mapping: exactly one task carries `Satisfies` mapping `AC-NO-CURRENT-MODE` — the plan's only `Satisfies`, carried by T-002, whose verification completes the plan's command set — and no other task carries `Satisfies`. Measured basis at this plan's commit: `validateSpecPlanCoverage` (`src/artifact/grammar.ts:2049`-2094) warns `change.acceptance-criterion-unmapped` for any criterion that is neither task-mapped nor close-bound, and errors `change.close-evidence-and-satisfied` on a `Satisfies` of a close-bound criterion; `isCloseBoundCriterion` (:2142) counts a criterion close-bound when it carries a complete `CloseEvidence` child; `AC-NO-CURRENT-MODE` is the only criterion of this spec without one, so it must be mapped and the other eight must not be; and `AC-CLOSE-LINT`'s `CloseEvidence` runs `--fail-on warnings`, which fails on any issue, so an unmapped `AC-NO-CURRENT-MODE` would make the bundle's own close unsatisfiable. This is the same reading the predecessor's ratified plan carried on the same engine.
T5 — the probes, discharged at plan time. The spec requires both directions demonstrated on throwaway copies before the artifact is approved; all were driven at this plan's commit against a prototype state carrying all three repairs (33 tests: the shipped 26 plus the seven synthetic direction tests), with every exit code read directly from the command: (R1) the prototype suite on the unmutated copy: 33 pass / 0 fail, exit 0; the hollowed copy (every `<Finding>` element of `findings.xml` renamed, root tags untouched): 32 pass / 1 fail, exit 1, the failure `findings.xml:Finding carries at least one element`, Received: undefined; the shipped suite on the same hollowed mutation: 26 pass / 0 fail, 1589 expect() calls, exit 0 — the zero-or-more swallow this repair closes. (R2) the discriminating copy — one direct `Entry` child carrying `layer="live"` had its `layer` attribute removed, `base` untouched: the shipped validator reports `record-retirement: ok` (exit 0) and the repaired suite is green (33 pass / 0 fail, exit 0), where the shipped predicate on the same mutated copy reds (25 pass / 1 fail, exit 1, Expected: 270, Received: 271) — the disagreement this repair removes; the repaired relation's own red direction — one live `Entry` removed entirely without re-persisting: the shipped validator stays silent (`record-retirement: ok`, exit 0, because `checkCeilingValue` compares only the live count against the ceiling) and the repaired suite reds (32 pass / 1 fail, exit 1, Expected: 270, Received: 271). (R3) the SNEAKY-shaped initializer (`const SNEAKY = (() => { const setup = "x"; return 195; })();`) referenced from the body by a benign comparison leaves the repaired guard red with the numeric-initializer finding (32 pass / 1 fail, exit 1, naming SNEAKY), where the shipped guard on the same shape is blind — its only red comes from the count comparison the guarded body itself makes (Expected: 195, Received: 271) while the shipped regression-guard test passes (25 pass / 1 fail, exit 1); the `async () => {` reformat of the pairing callback leaves the whole prototype suite green (33 pass / 0 fail, exit 0), where the shipped guard false-reds with the refusal (25 pass / 1 fail, exit 1, "the pairing test's body span could not be located; the guard refuses what it cannot prove"); the destructured and second-declarator bindings (`const { DESTRUCTED_PIN, UNREFERENCED_PIN } = { DESTRUCTED_PIN: 195, UNREFERENCED_PIN: 195 };` and `const FIRST_PIN = 195, SECOND_PIN = 195;`) referenced from the body leave the repaired guard red naming both DESTRUCTED_PIN and SECOND_PIN (32 pass / 1 fail, exit 1) with the unreferenced declarators out of scope (asserted by the synthetic directions in the same run), where the shipped suite was fully green (26 pass / 0 fail, exit 0); an unlocatable pairing callback leaves the repaired guard red with the refusal message (32 pass / 1 fail, exit 1); and the occupancy-table fixture written as real module-scope interface code reds the file the bundle itself ships (32 pass / 1 fail, exit 1, "occupancy-table shape expected: number in the file") — which is why the synthetic directions are crafted source text handed to the guard function, never real module-scope code in the delivered file: the shape duty is scoped anywhere in the file and needs no reference, so real fixture code would make the bundle unsatisfiable. These are authoring-time demonstrations; T-001 and T-002 re-drive their own during execution with tails in the executor's report, and each mutated copy's unmutated twin runs green in the same instrument.
T6 — assertion wiring. BaselineAssertions carry the shipped instruments green before the write — the retirement suite (67 pass / 0 fail, 1102 expect() calls at this plan's commit), the shipped validator (`record-retirement: ok`), `prove-record-preservation` and `validate-citation-anchors` (both `ok`) — plus `MustExist` for the repair file, the retirement suite, the seven record files and the spec; they red if the end state this bundle reads is broken before work starts. TargetAssertions carry the same set plus the repair's own suite — the close-bound criteria's CloseEvidence command — and the machine instrument for R3's removal clause: six `MustNotContain` entries over `src/artifact/xml.test.ts` naming the shipped scanner's identifiers (`function scanCode`, `function pairingBodySpan`, `function moduleBindingInitializer`, `NUMERIC_LITERAL_SHAPE`, `OCCUPANCY_TABLE_SHAPE`, `MODULE_BINDING_SHAPE`), so the removal clause is machine-checked at target and not a prose promise. The byte-invariance commands are task `Verification` (and close-only `CloseEvidence`) instruments with the named baseline `74f706aa1f26d95687c2fb23fa179351dfde9e33` (F210's named baseline; F215's window — this bundle's own diff; the predecessor's sanctioned supersede arrival and this bundle's own later archive arrival are the named exclusions), never TargetAssertions, in the house shape.

The executor emits its own execution-time cursor events for each task (opened with the epoch open at the task's start, progress, attempt on every verification cycle, command-run events from the target lint's `--run-commands`, verification-unavailable when evidence cannot be collected) inside the open epoch and does not omit them. T-001.Title: Land the digit-free non-vacuity assertion and the engine-aligned index predicate in the pairing test, and demonstrate the R1 and R2 probes on throwaway copies

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The pairing test's two repairs, in `src/artifact/xml.test.ts` only. The test named `pairs every element of the real record files at their committed bytes` keeps all of its other substance: the record-directory resolve from its own tree, all seven real record files parsed at their committed bytes with the shipped `parseGraceXmlArtifact`, non-null roots, `computeElementSpans` succeeding so every loud disagreement still raises, a span for every direct genre child, identity completeness and within-file uniqueness, cross-layer disjointness for the three genre pairs, index `Entry` elements self-closing, and the explicit generous timeout kept at `60_000` (F185). It gains exactly two changes. (R1) After the per-file node-list binding, the non-vacuity assertion in the spec's chartered digit-free form — destructure the first element of the bound list (`const [firstGenreChild] = nodes;`) and require it defined (`expect(firstGenreChild, \`${file}:${tag} carries at least one element\`).toBeDefined();`) — so every one of the seven record files' walked lists is required non-empty, with no numeric literal and no transcribed count in the form. (R2) The index-bookkeeping relation re-derived by exactly the shipped engine's predicate — every direct `Entry` child whose `layer` attribute is not `retired` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:996`) — compared against the persisted `base` read back through the shipped parser, with no `layer === "live"` filter left and no looser one. At T-001's boundary the shipped guard is still in place and stays green on the digit-free form (measured in the interim state: 26 pass / 0 fail, 2016 expect() calls, exit 0, on a throwaway copy). Failure: any numeric literal or transcribed record element count in the test's body, the non-emptiness assertion weakened to a subset of the files, or the predicate diverging from the engine's in either direction.

The R1 and R2 probes, demonstrated at plan-authoring time on throwaway copies (tails in the plan record, IntentSummary T5) and re-driven during execution on fresh throwaway copies — never against the committed tree, because neither suite takes a record path (IntentSummary T3), each mutated copy's unmutated twin run green in the same instrument. (a) R1 red: rename every `<Finding>` element of a copy's `findings.xml` to another tag (root open and close tags untouched) and run the suite inside the copy — it exits 1 naming the genre's non-emptiness, `findings.xml:Finding carries at least one element` with Received: undefined (driven at authoring: 32 pass / 1 fail, exit 1); the unmutated twin runs the same suite green. (b) R2 discriminating state: remove the `layer` attribute from one direct `Entry` child carrying `layer="live"` in a copy's `decisions.xml`, `base` untouched — the shipped validator stays green (`record-retirement: ok`, exit 0) and the repaired suite is green (driven: 33 pass / 0 fail, exit 0) where the shipped predicate reds on the same bytes (driven: 25 pass / 1 fail, exit 1, Expected: 270, Received: 271) — the disagreement this repair removes. (c) R2 red direction: remove one live `Entry` element entirely from a copy's `decisions.xml` without re-persisting the roots — the shipped validator stays silent (`record-retirement: ok`, exit 0; it never re-derives the persisted `base` against the metric) and the repaired suite reds on the `base` read-back (driven: 32 pass / 1 fail, exit 1, Expected: 270, Received: 271). No task boundary sits anywhere the record is not byte-identical to the spec's base commit.

T-002.Title: Replace the hand-rolled anti-occupancy guard with the parser-based guard over the imported TypeScript parser, ship the discriminating directions as synthetic self-tests, and demonstrate the R3 probes on throwaway copies

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The parser-based guard, in the same file. `antiOccupancyFailures` keeps its shipped signature and its real-file direction (the shipped regression-guard test reads the file's own source and expects an empty failure list). The implementation is over the TypeScript parser the file already imports (`import ts from "typescript"`, consumed today by `collectFromText` and after this task by the guard too), keyed on the count forms, binding on the pairing test's body shape, refusing what it cannot prove, with three detection duties in their widened forms: (i) any numeric literal inside the pairing test's callback body, read from the parser's numeric-literal nodes, so string and comment prose never fires, the `60_000` timeout argument outside the callback body never fires, and separator, exponent and hexadecimal forms are seen as numeric-literal nodes; (ii) the occupancy-table field shape anywhere in the file — a member named `expected` typed `number`, in interface/type-literal form and labeled-tuple form (`Array<[file: string, expected: number]>`, the shape the predecessor's table actually carried), while the same prose inside a string literal is not a hit; (iii) any module-scope binding with a numeric initializer referenced from the body — every declarator of every top-level variable statement visited, destructured names and non-first declarators included, and each initializer examined in full as an expression node, so a number behind an internal semicolon or brace is seen. Known boundary, stated rather than hidden (spec Goal R3): an identifier occurrence in the body — a property name included — counts as a reference (over-approximate, never under), and a locally shadowed name is not distinguished from an outer binding, the shipped word-boundary behavior retained. The hand-rolled scanner is gone with its lexer: `scanCode`, `pairingBodySpan`, `moduleBindingInitializer`, and the `NUMERIC_LITERAL_SHAPE`, `OCCUPANCY_TABLE_SHAPE`, `MODULE_BINDING_SHAPE` shapes removed — observed by the plan's six `MustNotContain` TargetAssertions over `src/artifact/xml.test.ts` (IntentSummary T6), machine-checked at target and not a prose promise. The refusal clause is kept: when the pairing test's callback cannot be located, the guard reports its refusal (the shipped message form, "the pairing test's body span could not be located; the guard refuses what it cannot prove") and never passes. Failure: any duty weakened or missing, the hand-rolled scanner surviving in any form, or the guard passing instead of refusing when it cannot locate the pairing test.

The synthetic directions. The suite ships the guard's discriminating directions as synthetic self-tests in the same file, all green at close: green on a pairing body with no numeric literals and no numeric module bindings; red on an inline numeric literal in the body; red on a numeric initializer behind an internal semicolon (the SNEAKY shape) referenced from the body; red on a destructured numeric binding and on a non-first-declarator numeric binding referenced from the body, and not red on the same statement's unreferenced declarator; red on the occupancy-table shape in interface/type-literal form and labeled-tuple form, and not red on its prose mention inside a string; green on an `async` callback; and the refusal message when the callback cannot be located. The fixtures are crafted source text handed to the guard function as strings, never real module-scope code in the delivered file — the discriminating reason, measured at authoring: the same fixture written as a real module-scope interface reds the file the bundle itself ships (32 pass / 1 fail, exit 1, "occupancy-table shape expected: number in the file"), because the shape duty is scoped anywhere in the file and needs no reference, so real fixture code would make the bundle unsatisfiable. Failure: any direction missing, weakened, or disagreeing with the real-file direction.

The R3 probes, discharged at plan-authoring time (tails in the plan record, IntentSummary T5) and re-driven during execution on throwaway copies of the repository, against the delivered file, each mutated copy's unmutated twin run green in the same instrument: (a) the SNEAKY-shaped initializer referenced from the body leaves the repaired guard red with the numeric-initializer finding (driven at authoring against the prototype guard: 32 pass / 1 fail, exit 1, naming SNEAKY), where the shipped guard is blind on the same shape — its pairing red comes only from the count comparison itself (driven shipped control: Expected: 195, Received: 271) while the shipped regression-guard test passes; (b) the `async () => {` reformat of the pairing callback leaves the whole suite green (driven: 33 pass / 0 fail, exit 0), where the shipped guard false-reds with the refusal (driven: 25 pass / 1 fail, exit 1); (c) the destructured and second-declarator bindings referenced from the body leave the repaired guard red naming both bindings (driven: 32 pass / 1 fail, exit 1, naming DESTRUCTED_PIN and SECOND_PIN, with the unreferenced declarators out of scope), where the shipped suite was fully green (driven: 26 pass / 0 fail, exit 0); (d) an unlocatable pairing callback leaves the repaired guard red with the refusal message (driven: 32 pass / 1 fail, exit 1). No probe runs against the committed tree or the production record.
